root_cause.FINAL: AIDY requires 1700 minutes of M1 history to build H1/H4/D1 aggregates and is missing 1681 of them. Each scheduled capture performs ONE bounded M1 read reused across timeframes, which can build 15m but never 1h/4h/1d. Completeness thresholds require 1.00 coverage on every timeframe, so all_timeframes_ready is always false, so every snapshot is 'partial', so market_reference_not_complete, so AIDY never reaches the model.
root_cause.the_fix: Enable AIDY_TWELVE_DATA_BOOTSTRAP_ENABLED and run the historical M1 ingest (twelve_data_bootstrap.py, POST /day53/twelve-data-bootstrap). The Phase B rollout workflow deploys with this flag set to 'false', which is why the backfill has never run.
root_cause.quota_is_NOT_the_blocker: Internal ceiling is 720/day rolling 24h. Usage on 2026-09-14 was 53 rolling, 0 for the day; peak day ever 202. A capture costs 1 credit. Earlier quota hypothesis was WRONG.
root_cause.cron_was_a_real_but_separate_fault: Cron genuinely was not firing between 2026-09-13T10:36 and the redeploy. Fixed.
root_cause.weekend_note: Sunday capture is CORRECT behaviour. Do not treat weekend activity as a fault.

m1_publication_lag_fix.root_cause: Twelve Data publishes each closed M1 bar ~64s after close (63.8-64.0s, zero variance across 9 captures). Market capture ran ~3s past each 5-minute boundary and evaluated the just-closed bucket, whose final minute was not yet published. interval_due's due window closes at +60s; the data arrives at +64s. It missed by four seconds, every time, forever.
m1_publication_lag_fix.fix: interval_due gains offset_seconds; market capture uses 120s. Bucket boundaries, coverage thresholds and PIT semantics untouched - only the sampling instant moved.
m1_publication_lag_fix.cron_change: Required, not optional. Due windows sit at minute %% 5 == 2 and the old */2 + 5,15,25,35,45,55 schedule had no tick in half of them, so an offset alone would have silently HALVED capture. Now '* * * * *'. Invocations 864 -> 1440/day; useful captures unchanged at 288/day.
m1_publication_lag_fix.cohort_impact: Reset the active forward cohort under the Day 53 evidence-semantic rule. Reset cost was zero - the cohort held no model-resolved decisions. This was the cheapest moment the change could ever be made.
m1_publication_lag_fix.remaining_blocker: 4h coverage 0.500. NOT a timing fault - the 4h bucket rolled to 08:00-12:00 and needs 240 minutes of M1 history the backfill never finished (the hardened bootstrap failed at 11:21, almost certainly because it could not prove all_timeframes_ready through this very bug). Re-dispatched after the fix.
